source.title: How Data Scales in Agentic Reinforcement Learning: Laws and Synthesis Strategies
source.authors: Bo-Wei He; Yan-Kai Chen; Xiao-Kun Zhang; Chang-Jiang Han; Ye Yuan; Chong Li; Xue Liu

record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling relations and compute-budget allocation in agentic reinforcement learning, a training regime distinct from text pretraining.
record.gate_note: The study uses held-out task success transformed to L = −log psuccess as a loss-equivalent metric; it does not measure held-out pretraining cross-entropy. It reports its own scaling sweeps, fit sensitivities, and allocation validation. Results cited from prior work are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study fits its own power laws of a loss-equivalent metric (−log held-out success) in agentic RL post-training. It covers data axes (environment, task, trajectory) and model size (0.6B–32B), derives a compute-optimal allocation, and validates it at a held-out scale 4× larger. This is a new training regime with results on the power-law form (V5), allocation (V3), extrapolation (V2) and fit-dependence (V7). It measures no pretraining cross-entropy.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude agentic-RL data is a structured design space, not a scalar. Environment > task > trajectory exponents hold in all 21 settings; they claim the ordering, not the values. Their cost-aware recipe predicts a held-out 14B run at 32C0 and gives 1.4–1.7× compute efficiency over the tested alternatives. Unlike Chinchilla, data budgets grow faster than model size (0.74 vs 0.26).
record.recipe_differences: The study uses agentic-RL training and held-out task success transformed to −log success, rather than next-token pretraining and held-out cross-entropy. It decomposes data into task, environment, and trajectory cardinalities and optimizes their budgets alongside model size.
record.method_sensitivity: Exponents vary across model families, domains, model sizes, and algorithms; the compute allocation shifts with domain-specific and refined cost models. Task-environment interactions affect returns, and content-only environment variation has a smaller fitted exponent. Within the reported Math+Code sensitivity checks, alternative task definitions and held-axis values preserve the exponent ordering.

fits_no_version.finding: Synthesis discount factors κ (0.31–0.71) and axis-specific collapse ratios r* (9.4, 3.4, 1.4) for synthetic-to-real data mixes (Table 3, Sec 5, Appendix I–J).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Synthetic data's real-equivalent yield and collapse threshold differ systematically by data axis in agentic RL.

fits_no_version.finding: Collapsing the three axes into one weighted scalar data axis fits far worse (R² 0.83 vs 0.978) (Appendix O).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In agentic RL, data cannot be reduced to a single scalar quantity for scaling-law purposes.

record.problems: The measured loss is a proxy based on held-out benchmark success rather than cross-entropy. Experiments cover specific model families, benchmarks, and sub-frontier scales; the held-out allocation validation is one compute scale and one model size. The study notes task-environment non-orthogonality, limited world counts, a finite configured structure inventory, and cost-model dependence.
record.rows_left_out: Kept 51 rows, below the 60-row limit. Omitted additional sensitivity and synthesis-pricing results (including synthesis-method-specific discounts and collapse ratios), reward-density fits, detailed world-split success values, and cost-model perturbation table entries because they do not directly measure the listed claim versions or were lower priority than the main scaling, interaction, and allocation findings.

untested.parts: All: no pretraining cross-entropy is measured.
Extrapolation over orders of magnitude (only 4× compute tested), and extrapolation of pretraining loss.
Pretraining parameter/token split as defined by Kaplan or Hoffmann.
All: no depth/width comparison at fixed parameter count.
Image/video modalities, repeated-data pretraining, supervised fine-tuning and transfer.
All: no downstream-vs-pretraining-loss relation (the loss metric is itself task success).

missing.what: Training-budget convention changes ατ: 0.11 by default, 0.08 under a token cap, 0.07 iso-FLOP. αE and αT move ≤0.01.
Fixing L∞ at 0/0.10/0.15 gives exponents (0.36,0.23,0.10)/(0.41,0.26,0.11)/(0.44,0.28,0.12). A shared-L∞ joint fit and a Levenberg-Marquardt refit agree within 0.006.
Choice of metric matters: raw success fits poorly (R² < 0.85); logit gives exponents differing by a constant factor.
Recipe exponents per domain (Table 20) and under ±50% cost perturbations (Table 21, max shift 0.048).
Local log-log slopes per segment (env 0.44→0.36, task 0.29→0.22, traj 0.14→0.08) and 6- vs 8-point fits.

record.verdict_notes: The loss is −log held-out task success after RL post-training, not cross-entropy, so V1/V2/V3 bear only by analogy. r44/r45 compare the study's own method with baselines and are delinked. The Chinchilla-transferred baseline is the authors' construct, not a test of Hoffmann et al.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining cross-entropy loss is measured.
Tests extrapolation of the loss-equivalent agentic-RL metric, not cross-entropy; the held-out compute point is 4 times the largest compute level used to fit, not orders of magnitude larger.
Tests compute-optimal allocation across agentic-RL environment, task, trajectory, and model-size budgets, not the conventional pretraining parameter-count/token-count split.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Tests agentic RL, not image/video modalities, repeated-data pretraining, fine-tuning, or transfer.
No test of downstream-task performance as a function of pretraining loss.
Examines setup and fitting sensitivity in agentic RL; it does not compare the original sources' pretraining fits directly.

rows.subject: Qwen3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Fit a cross-axis interaction correction to the environment-task scaling surface
rows.measure: Cross-axis interaction; low environment diversity makes increasing task count yield almost no gain; correction-fit R2
rows.note: Shows the independent-axis power-law description needs qualification when task and environment diversity interact.
rows.check: The additive independent-axis power law fits with R² 0.93 and needs an interaction term to reach 0.98. Per-axis power laws still hold.

source_check.correct: R² increases from 0.93 to 0.98 with γ=0.18 and β=0.21 at fixed Dτ=8. Partial describes the independent additive approximation; dependence on the joint-axis setting is observed for V7.
source_check.problem: A shared partial state does not distinguish the incomplete independent-axis approximation from observed V7 setup dependence.

rows.subject: Qwen3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Fit loss-equivalent exponents over a parameter-count sweep
rows.measure: Fitted model-size exponent αN
rows.note: Authors state that the frontier-scale extrapolation is unverified.
rows.check: The subject is the Qwen3 series from 0.6B to 32B, not Qwen3-8B. αN is a parameter-count power law that feeds the allocation; it is not itself an allocation result, so the V3 link is dropped.

rows.subject: Qwen3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Compute-constrained allocation fit across six IsoFLOP levels
rows.measure: Fitted compute exponents for optimal environment, task, trajectory, and model size budgets
rows.note: This is an agentic-RL allocation over data cardinalities and model size, rather than a parameter/token pretraining split.
rows.check: The exponents come from numerically solving the Lagrangian on the fitted laws, then fitting across C. Empirical grid-search optima at six IsoFLOP levels are plotted in Fig. 5a. It is an allocation result, not a V5 power-law-in-loss row.

source_check.correct: Subject: Qwen3 compute-allocation recipe with model size N varying, using default Qwen3-8B data-axis coefficients and a separate model-size fit. Reported exponents are 0.34, 0.27, 0.13 and 0.26.
source_check.locator_found: Sections 6.1–6.2, Equation 8, Figure 5a; Appendices E and K
source_check.problem: The allocation law optimizes model size across compute budgets; it is not a result confined to a fixed Qwen3-8B checkpoint.

rows.subject: Qwen3-14B
rows.operation_detail: Train at the allocation predicted from fits on smaller compute levels and model sizes
rows.measure: Held-out task success and prediction agreement
rows.note: The held-out test is at a compute level four times the largest level used for fitting; 116 allocation units reused structure on different worlds because only 384 signatures were available.
rows.check: Extrapolation is 4× compute beyond the fit, plus a held-out model size. The predicted value is 51.7% in Sec 6.3 but 51.1% in Sec 6.2.

source_check.correct: Observed allocation validation for V3: predicted success 51.7% ± 1.6%, measured 51.3% ± 1.4%, three seeds, at 32C0 after fitting through 8C0. V2's orders-of-magnitude extrapolation is cannot_determine because the compute extension is only 4×.
source_check.locator_found: Section 6.3; Section 6.2 gives a conflicting prediction of 51.1%
source_check.problem: Observed overstates the evidence for V2's explicitly multi-order extrapolation requirement.

rows.subject: Qwen3-8B

rows.subject: Qwen3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Compare a single-axis power-law fit to alternative fitting choices and interaction forms
rows.measure: Model-selection comparison for per-axis loss fits
rows.baseline: Single-term form favored by BIC at every measured scale
rows.note: The paper reports no support for a two-regime fit over the measured ranges.
rows.check: A single-term power law is preferred by BIC. For V7's 'curves bend away' clause this means no bending was found over the measured ranges. The state reads as observed for V5 and as not showing bending for V7.

source_check.correct: Single-term offset power laws are favored by BIC at every measured scale: observed for V5; no supported two-regime bending in these measurements for the curvature component of V7.
source_check.problem: Observed is appropriate for V5, but not for the linked V7 bending component.

source_check.reason: The joint surface qualifies a simple independent additive extension: an interaction improves R² from 0.93 to 0.98. The weaker content-only exponent alone does not limit V5, since it remains a fitted power law.
